_comment: Real defects with known ground truth. Every one of these actually occurred and was independently confirmed during the 2026-08-17 Pi-Dev-Ops release-gate session. Ground truth is what the defect IS, not a description a model could pattern-match from the prompt. A model scores only by naming the mechanism.

cases.code:
set -uo pipefail
PY_OK=0
if [ -f app/requirements.txt ]; then
  [ "$MODE_FULL" = 1 ] && "$PY" -m pip install -q -r app/requirements.txt >>"$LOG" 2>&1
  if "$PY" -c "import fastapi, pydantic" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then PY_OK=1; gate "deps-python" true
  else skip "deps-python" "deps not importable - run --full or activate the venv"; fi
fi
# later: a SKIP does not increment FAIL, so VERDICT prints READY and exit is 0
cases.question: This is a CI definition-of-done gate. --full is documented as 'real dependency install'. Find the most serious defect.
cases.ground_truth: The pip install's exit status is discarded. Under --full a FAILED install falls through to the import check, reports SKIP rather than FAIL, and the run still prints READY with exit 0 - a false green. Real trigger: PEP-668 externally-managed-environment makes pip exit 1 outside a venv.

cases.source: watchdog written during the same session (real)
cases.code:
W=/tmp/review/reviewer-report.json
while true; do
  if [ -f "$W" ]; then echo "REPORT_WRITTEN"; exit 0; fi
  if ! pgrep -f "claude -p --model sonnet" >/dev/null; then echo "REVIEWER_DIED"; exit 1; fi
  sleep 15
done
cases.question: This watchdog is supposed to detect when the reviewer process dies. Find the defect that makes it unable to do so.
cases.ground_truth: pgrep -f matches against full command lines, and this script's OWN command line contains the literal pattern 'claude -p --model sonnet'. So pgrep always finds at least itself, the died-branch can never fire, and a dead reviewer looks identical to a running one forever.

cases.question: This extracts a review report from an LLM response that may contain chain-of-thought. The system prompt shown to the model included a literal schema example containing "verdict":"PASS|FAIL". What goes wrong?
cases.ground_truth: Reasoning models echo the schema template inside their thinking. Because the selector keeps the LAST parsing object, it selects the echoed template (verdict 'PASS|FAIL') instead of the real report, silently converting a genuine FAIL-with-findings into a PASS. Needs a validity check that a real verdict is exactly PASS or FAIL.

cases.source: a wrapped CLI call in the same session (real)
cases.code:
run_review() {
  codex exec --sandbox workspace-write - < brief 2>&1 | tail -40
}
run_review
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "review OK, proceeding to push"
fi
cases.question: The reviewer printed 'ERROR: You've hit your usage limit' and wrote no report, yet this code proceeded. Explain every mechanism that let that happen.
cases.ground_truth: Two compounding faults. First, the pipe to tail means $? is tail's status, not codex's - a pipeline masks the real exit code (needs PIPESTATUS or set -o pipefail). Second, and more fundamental, exit status is the wrong success signal: the check should assert the ARTIFACT exists (the report file), because a tool can exit 0 while producing nothing.
